extracted.intended_audience: applicants, patent practitioners, and patent illustrators preparing U.S. utility, design, or plant patent application drawings
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards from 37 CFR 1.84 governing preparation, content, format, and submission of drawings and photographs for U.S. patent applications (utility, design, and plant). Covers acceptable media, paper/size/margins, views, labeling, lettering, shading, symbols, and other drawing conventions and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings — acceptable categories (black ink; color)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two acceptable categories for presenting drawings in utility and design patent applications: (1) Black ink: Black and white drawings are normally required. India ink, or its equivalent that secures solid black lines, must be used for drawings; or (2) Color: Color drawings are permitted in design applications. On rare occasions, color drawings may be necessary as the only practical medium by which to disclose the subject matter sought to be patented in a utility patent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Color drawings: specification must include certain reference language and the application must include the number of sets required by the rule. Color drawings must be of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible in black and white in the printed patent. Color drawings are not permitted in international applications (PCT Rule 11.13). The Office will accept color drawings in utility applications only after granting a petition that includes: the fee (§ 1.17(h)); one set of color drawings if submitted electronically (or three sets if not); and an amendment inserting specified language as the first paragraph of the brief description of the drawings. See paragraphs (a)(2)(i)–(iii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Photographs — black and white and color
rubrics_metrics.description: Photographs, including photocopies of photographs, are not ordinarily permitted in utility and design patent applications but will be accepted if photographs are the only practicable medium for illustrating the claimed invention (e.g., electrophoresis gels, blots, autoradiographs, cell cultures, histological tissue cross sections, animals, plants, in vivo imaging, TLC plates, crystalline structures, and ornamental effects in design applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Photographs must be of sufficient quality so that all details are reproducible in the printed patent. If the subject admits illustration by a drawing, the examiner may require a drawing instead. Color photographs will be accepted if the conditions for color drawings and black and white photographs are satisfied (see paragraphs (a)(2) and (b)(1)). Photographs must be developed on paper meeting the sheet-size and margin requirements of the rule (see paragraphs (f) and (g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifying indicia should be provided, and if provided, should include the title of the invention, inventor's name, and application number, or docket number (if any) if an application number has not been assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identification information is provided, it must be placed on the front of each sheet within the top margin. Each drawing sheet submitted after the filing date must be identified as either 'Replacement Sheet' or 'New Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d). Marked-up copies of amended drawing figures with annotations must be clearly labeled as 'Annotated Sheet' pursuant to § 1.121(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic forms in drawings (chemical/mathematical formulae, tables, waveforms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Chemical or mathematical formulae, tables, and waveforms may be submitted as drawings, and are subject to the same requirements as drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each chemical or mathematical formula must be labeled as a separate figure, using brackets when necessary, to show proper integration. Each group of waveforms must be presented as a single figure, using a common vertical axis with time along the horizontal axis. Each individual waveform discussed in the specification must be identified with a separate letter designation adjacent to the vertical axis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings submitted to the Office must be made on paper which is flexible, strong, white, smooth, non-shiny, and durable. All sheets must be reasonably free from cracks, creases, and folds. Only one side of the sheet may be used for the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sheet must be reasonably free from erasures and must be free from alterations, overwritings, and interlineations. Photographs must be developed on paper meeting the sheet-size (§ 1.84(f)) and margin (§ 1.84(g)) requirements. See paragraph (b) for additional photograph requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Size of paper
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawing sheets in an application must be the same size. One of the shorter sides of the sheet is regarded as its top. The size of the sheets on which drawings are made must be: (1) 21.0 cm by 29.7 cm (DIN size A4), or (2) 21.6 cm by 27.9 cm (8 1/2 by 11 inches).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistency in sheet size is required across all drawing sheets in the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Margins and sight area
rubrics_metrics.description: The sheets must not contain frames around the sight (i.e., the usable surface), but should have scan target points (i.e., cross-hairs) printed on two catercorner margin corners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each sheet must include a top margin of at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), left side margin of at least 2.5 cm (1 inch), right side margin of at least 1.5 cm (5/8 inch), and bottom margin of at least 1.0 cm (3/8 inch), leaving a sight no greater than 17.0 cm by 26.2 cm on A4 sheets and no greater than 17.6 cm by 24.4 cm on 8 1/2 by 11 inch sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Views — general requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawing must contain as many views as necessary to show the invention. The views may be plan, elevation, section, or perspective views. Detail views of portions of elements, on a larger scale if necessary, may also be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All views of the drawing must be grouped together and arranged on the sheet(s) without wasting space, preferably in an upright position, clearly separated from one another, and must not be included in the sheets containing the specifications, claims, or abstract. Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines. Waveforms of electrical signals may be connected by dashed lines to show relative timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploded views
rubrics_metrics.description: Exploded views, with the separated parts embraced by a bracket, to show the relationship or order of assembly of various parts are permissible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an exploded view is on the same sheet as another figure, the exploded view should be placed in brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial views and linking across sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: When necessary, a view of a large machine or device in its entirety may be broken into partial views on a single sheet, or extended over several sheets if there is no loss in facility of understanding the view.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views drawn on separate sheets must always be capable of being linked edge to edge so that no partial view contains parts of another partial view. A smaller scale view should be included showing the whole formed by the partial views and indicating the positions of the parts shown. When a portion is enlarged, the view and the enlarged view must each be labeled as separate views. Where views on two or more sheets form a single complete view, the views must be arranged so the complete figure can be assembled without concealing any part. Very long views may be divided into parts placed one above the other on a single sheet provided the relationship between parts is clear and unambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sectional views (hatching and designation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The plane upon which a sectional view is taken should be indicated on the view from which the section is cut by a broken line. Ends of the broken line should be designated by Arabic or Roman numerals corresponding to the view number and have arrows indicating the direction of sight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hatching must be used to indicate section portions, made by regularly spaced oblique parallel lines spaced sufficiently apart to be distinguished. Hatching should not impede reading of reference characters; if necessary, break off hatching where reference characters are inserted. Hatching must be at a substantial angle to surrounding axes, preferably 45°. Cross sections must show all materials as in the view from which the section was taken. Parts in cross section must show proper materials by hatching; juxtaposed different elements must be hatched differently. For large areas, hatching may be confined to an edging. Different types of hatching should have different conventional meanings regarding materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate positions and moved positions
rubrics_metrics.description: A moved position may be shown by a broken line superimposed upon a suitable view if this can be done without crowding; otherwise, a separate view must be used for this purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use broken lines for moved positions only when not crowding the drawing; otherwise include separate views.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modified forms of construction
rubrics_metrics.description: Modified forms of construction must be shown in separate views.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional guidance beyond requirement to show modified forms separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrangement of views on sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: One view must not be placed upon another or within the outline of another. All views on the same sheet should stand in the same direction and, if possible, so that they can be read with the sheet held in an upright position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If views wider than the sheet are necessary, the sheet may be turned on its side so the top of the sheet is on the right-hand side. Words must appear in a horizontal, left-to-right fashion when page is upright or turned so top becomes the right side, except for graphs using standard scientific convention to denote axes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Front page view (selection for front page)
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the views should be suitable for inclusion on the front page of the patent application publication and patent as the illustration of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may suggest a single view (by figure number) for inclusion on the front page. Views must not be connected by projection lines and must not contain center lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scale
rubrics_metrics.description: The scale to which a drawing is made must be large enough to show the mechanism without crowding when the drawing is reduced in size to two-thirds in reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indications such as 'actual size' or 'scale 1/2' on the drawings are not permitted since these lose their meaning with reproduction in a different format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character of lines, numbers, and letters
rubrics_metrics.description: All drawings must be made by a process which will give them satisfactory reproduction characteristics. Every line, number, and letter must be durable, clean, black (except for color drawings), sufficiently dense and dark, and uniformly thick and well-defined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Weight of all lines and letters must be heavy enough for adequate reproduction. Applies to all lines however fine, to shading, and to lines representing cut surfaces. Lines and strokes of different thicknesses may be used where different thicknesses have different meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shading
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of shading in views is encouraged if it aids in understanding the invention and if it does not reduce legibility. Shading is used to indicate the surface or shape of spherical, cylindrical, and conical elements; flat parts may also be lightly shaded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Spaced lines for shading are preferred; they must be thin and as few as practicable and contrast with the rest of the drawings. Heavy lines on the shade side can substitute, except where they superimpose or obscure reference characters. Light should come from the upper left corner at a 45° angle. Surface delineations should preferably be shown by proper shading. Solid black shading areas are not permitted, except for bar graphs or color.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: Graphical drawing symbols may be used for conventional elements when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elements for which symbols are used must be adequately identified in the specification. Known devices should be illustrated by symbols with universally recognized conventional meaning. Other non-universal symbols may be used subject to Office approval if they are not likely to be confused with conventional symbols and are readily identifiable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legends
rubrics_metrics.description: Suitable descriptive legends may be used subject to approval by the Office, or may be required by the examiner where necessary for understanding of the drawing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legends should contain as few words as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers, letters, and reference characters — general rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference characters (numerals are preferred), sheet numbers, and view numbers must be plain and legible, and must not be used in association with brackets or inverted commas, or enclosed within outlines (e.g., encircled). They must be oriented in the same direction as the view so as to avoid having to rotate the sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters should follow the profile of the object depicted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters and alphabets usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The English alphabet must be used for letters, except where another alphabet is customarily used (e.g., Greek alphabet for angles, wavelengths, mathematical formulas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further guidance beyond allowed customary exceptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum size and placement of characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Numbers, letters, and reference characters must measure at least 0.32 cm (1/8 inch) in height. They should not be placed so as to interfere with comprehension, should not cross or mingle with lines, and should not be placed upon hatched or shaded surfaces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When necessary (e.g., indicating a surface or cross section), a reference character may be underlined and a blank space left in hatching where the character occurs so it appears distinct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of reference characters
rubrics_metrics.description: The same part of an invention appearing in more than one view of the drawing must always be designated by the same reference character, and the same reference character must never be used to designate different parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference characters not mentioned in the description shall not appear in the drawings. Reference characters mentioned in the description must appear in the drawings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Lead lines are those lines between the reference characters and the details referred to. Such lines may be straight or curved and should be as short as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead lines must originate in the immediate proximity of the reference character and extend to the feature indicated. Lead lines must not cross each other. Lead lines are required for each reference character except for those which indicate the surface or cross section on which they are placed (such reference characters must be underlined). Lead lines must be executed in the same way as lines in the drawing (see paragraph (l)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows
rubrics_metrics.description: Arrows may be used at the ends of the lines, provided that their meaning is clear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable uses include: (1) on a lead line, a freestanding arrow to indicate the entire section towards which it points; (2) on a lead line, an arrow touching a line to indicate the surface shown by the line looking along the direction of the arrow; (3) to show the direction of movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright or mask work notice in drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: A copyright or mask work notice may appear in the drawing, but must be placed within the sight of the drawing immediately below the figure representing the copyrighted or mask work material and be limited to letters 0.32 cm to 0.64 cm (1/8 to 1/4 inches) high.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content of the notice must be limited to elements provided for by law (e.g., '© 1983 John Doe' or '*M* John Doe'). Inclusion of such notice will be permitted only if the authorization language set forth in § 1.71(e) is included at the beginning of the specification (preferably first paragraph).

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of sheets of drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Sheets of drawings should be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, starting with 1, within the sight as defined in paragraph (g). These numbers, if present, must be placed in the middle of the top of the sheet, but not in the margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers can be placed on the right-hand side if the drawing extends too close to the middle top. The drawing sheet numbering must be clear and larger than numbers used as reference characters. The number of each sheet should be shown by two Arabic numerals placed on either side of an oblique line, with the first being the sheet number and the second being the total number of sheets, with no other marking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbering of views
rubrics_metrics.description: The different views must be numbered in consecutive Arabic numerals, starting with 1, independent of the numbering of the sheets and, if possible, in the order in which they appear on the drawing sheet(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Partial views intended to form one complete view, on one or several sheets, must be identified by the same number followed by a capital letter. View numbers must be preceded by the abbreviation 'FIG.' Where only a single view is used, it must not be numbered and the abbreviation 'FIG.' must not appear. Numbers and letters identifying the views must be simple and clear and not used with brackets, circles, or inverted commas. View numbers must be larger than numbers used for reference characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security markings
rubrics_metrics.description: Authorized security markings may be placed on the drawings provided they are outside the sight, preferably centered in the top margin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security markings must be outside usable drawing area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections on drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any corrections on drawings submitted to the Office must be durable and permanent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrections should not be ephemeral — they must be made in a durable manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holes in drawing sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: No holes should be made by applicant in the drawing sheets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not punch, staple, or otherwise perforate drawing sheets submitted to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of drawings (cross-references)
rubrics_metrics.description: References to specialized drawing types: see § 1.152 for design drawings, § 1.1026 for international design reproductions, § 1.165 for plant drawings, and § 1.173(a)(2) for reissue drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rule points to other sections for requirements specific to certain drawing types (design, plant, international design reproductions, reissue).
